A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central results, and proofs. The main texts and appendices support reliable comparison. v1’s numerical eigenfunction approximation section is retained as Appendix B in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, analytic kernel examples, and numerical approximation guidance, but no original empirical outcomes. Appendix A contains a proof; the cited Burgers and Navier–Stokes experiments belong to earlier work.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original simulations for learning Poisson and heat solution operators, including estimator comparisons and covariance-smoothness experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions query the covariance kernel’s leading eigenfunctions and construct the same linear estimator in Section 3.1.1. v2 applies this method experimentally without introducing a new component or changing its procedure.

E1.justification: v2 introduces actual evaluation on two-dimensional Poisson forcing-to-solution and heat initial-condition-to-solution tasks, using synthetic Gaussian-process inputs and varying covariance smoothness. v1 has no corresponding empirical coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons against passive least squares and passive Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) in Figures 1 and 3. Appendix C additionally evaluates FNO trained on actively collected data. v1 evaluates no comparators.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce 64 × 64 grids, 100-function test sets, training-sample-size sweeps, and mean-squared relative error. The heat experiment targets t = 1 using 1000 forward-time discretization steps. These are newly introduced protocols, not revisions to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Figures 2 and 4 introduce covariance-smoothness sensitivity studies, including γ ≤ 1 cases outside the stated convergence guarantee. Appendix C tests FNO with active training inputs and documents its poor performance. Neither analysis appears in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. v2’s new figures show error curves without error bars or uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: v2 adds all empirical results in Figures 1–6. They show substantially lower active-linear errors at larger training sizes, faster convergence with greater covariance smoothness, and high or erratic active-FNO errors. These are new findings; v1 contains no corresponding empirical scores.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Theorems 1–2 and their proofs, kernel-rate derivations, and Proposition 1 with its Appendix A proof remain unchanged. The numerical eigenfunction approximation mathematics is relocated to Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1, and discussion retain the same central claims: covariance-dependent active convergence rates, arbitrarily fast reducible-error decay, and a non-vanishing passive minimax lower bound.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly suggests that FNO fails on active inputs because training and test distributions differ. Section 5.1 also distinguishes observed convergence for γ ≤ 1 from the formal γ > 1 guarantee. These provide limited new applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link and experimental implementation information, including Gaussian-process parameters, finite-difference solvers, grid resolution, heat discretization, and FNO layer and Fourier-mode counts. v1 provides no corresponding experimental recipe or code link; its eigenfunction approximation guidance is retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and research positioning in Sections 1.2 and 3.3 remain unchanged. FNO was already cited in v1; its new experimental participation does not revise the paper’s novelty claims or related-work account.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and organization are retained. v2 inserts an experimental Section 5 and Appendix C, moves the former Section 5 to Appendix B, and changes the introductory domain notation from Ω to X. There is no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 introduces six figures where v1 has none, adding paired linear/log-scale comparisons and smoothness-sensitivity plots. Figures 5–6 redisplay the main comparison curves with active-FNO results added. Figure 6 appears under the heat subsection despite its erroneous Poisson caption.

improvement.justification: The new Poisson and heat simulations provide useful practical support for the retained theoretical proposal. Smoothness studies and the active-FNO failure analysis clarify its empirical scope, while implementation settings and a code link help reproducibility. The gain is limited by incomplete FNO training details and absent run-level uncertainty reporting; the central theoretical contribution remains unchanged.
